newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica in mourning for former leader Manley.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica in mourning for former leader Manley.

text.p: Flags flew at half staff across Jamaica on Saturday as the country mourned the death of former prime minister Michael Manley.
The government announced that three days of official mourning would begin next Friday. Manley's body will lie in state at the National Arena in Kingston from then until Sunday, it said.
The funeral will take place on Sunday, March 16 at the Holy Trinity Cathedral.

Manley, a legendary figure in Caribbean politics and a prominent campaigner for the Third World on the international stage, died on Thursday night at his home after a long battle with cancer. He was 72.
The scion of a Jamaican political family, he was prime minister from 1972 to 1980 then again from 1989 until 1992 when he retired because of his failing health.
With news of his death, tributes have poured in from colleagues, political opponents and world leaders.
Jamaican television and radio stations have been dominated by his passing, dedicating programmes to replaying old interviews and speeches.
